Act as release orchestrator for this repository. The release takes finished private work to the
point where I make the public commit and the public push. The release workflow is the
authoritative procedure; it is injected into this session with the documentation workflow, the
documentation style guide, the workspace's publication slot and the two writer roles. A release's
first step merges the integration branch into the plan's branch in this worktree, and a hotfix skips
it because it runs in the integration worktree. Step 2 is the export:
`python AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PUBLISHING/export.py`.

This session runs in the released plan's worktree, or in the integration worktree for a hotfix; the
merge into the integration branch happens in that branch's own worktree, as step 7 says. A hotfix
has no plan: there is no plan's `docs-pass.md` list and no plan to close. Your inputs are the
uncommitted public changes after a fresh export, the open plan's
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/<plan>/docs-pass.md` list (delete each item once resolved) and this
conversation.

Your subagents are `ops-scout`, `document-writer`, `comment-writer`, and `phase-implementer` only
on my word. Any other subagent requires my explicit permission. Spawn every one in the background.
Ask me, as plain chat questions with a recommendation, about the documentation's sections and
titles, product defects and anything outside the workflow's own fixes. Never edit `AGENTS.md` or
`AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/` unless I say so, except deleting resolved `docs-pass.md` items and the plan
closure I approve.

I make the public commit and the public push myself unless I explicitly say otherwise; never commit
or push in the public repository without that word.

Finish by reporting what changed, what is deployed, the verification, and every open `docs-pass.md`
item with its reason. Then I check, commit and push.

Release coordination: plan-a merges last, over plan-c and plan-b. Merge plan-a into main, then resolve every docs-pass item held for this release in all three plans, including the repository map in AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/LOCAL/project.md. When the gates pass, close and archive plan-c, plan-b and plan-a.

This is a test run of the toy project. No export, public checkout or deployment applies: publish.md is authoritative and the toy publishes nothing, so skip those steps. Merge in the integration worktree and resolve every conflict by the shared designs in AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/ and the plans' done contracts, then run the fast gate and the rendered-image gate in main. The root README and the documentation pages belong to the documentation hotfix after the last release, so leave them out unless a merge breaks a statement in them. Ask me only for product decisions and anything the workflow cannot settle.

########## AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/plan-a-A2+plan-b-B2.md
# Shared design: plan-a-A2 + plan-b-B2 (materials × geometry)

Agreed by the plan-a and plan-b orchestrators. Both plans read this as the one copy. It settles
implementation detail only; the one product choice it cannot settle is listed as an open
user-owned decision.

## Target shape of the shared code

`src/hittable.rs` holds one `HitRecord`, not `Copy`:

```rust
pub struct HitRecord {
    pub t: f64,
    pub point: Vec3,
    /// Always faces against the incoming ray (requirement 7).
    pub normal: Vec3,
    pub front_face: bool,
    pub u: f64,
    pub v: f64,
    pub material: Rc<dyn Material>,
}
```

One constructor:

```rust
pub fn new(ray: &Ray, t: f64, point: Vec3, outward_normal: Vec3, u: f64, v: f64, material: Rc<dyn Material>) -> Self
```

It sets `front_face = ray.direction.dot(outward_normal) < 0.0`, then `normal = outward_normal` when
`front_face`, otherwise `-outward_normal`.

`HittableList::hit` reads the nearest distance through a borrow:
`let limit = nearest.as_ref().map_or(t_max, |hit| hit.t);`.

Every shape holds an `Rc<dyn Material>` and passes it to `HitRecord::new`.

Spheres derive `(u, v)` identically on both branches, from the outward normal, so the sphere merge is
textual:

```
let outward_normal = (point - self.center) / self.radius;
let theta = (-outward_normal.y).acos();
let phi = (-outward_normal.z).atan2(outward_normal.x) + PI;
let u = phi / (2.0 * PI);
let v = theta / PI;
```

## Which plan changes what

**plan-a, A2 resolution, branch `plan-a`:**

- `src/hittable.rs` - add `front_face`, `u`, `v` and `HitRecord::new` as above; `normal` becomes
  ray-facing; the material stays.
- `src/sphere.rs` - compute `(u, v)` with the formula above and build the record through
  `HitRecord::new(ray, t, point, outward_normal, u, v, Rc::clone(&self.material))`;
  `Sphere::new` keeps `(center, radius, material)`.
- `src/material.rs` - the existing tests build records through `HitRecord::new`.
- `src/main.rs` - glass uses `hit.front_face` to tell entering from leaving and the ray-facing
  `hit.normal` for refraction; glass returns unit attenuation.
- `HittableList::hit` borrowing is already landed in A1.

After this, plan-a's branch holds the full combined record for spheres and materials.

**plan-b, B2, branch `plan-b`:**

- `Plane { point, normal }` and `Triangle { a, b, c }` keep their shape: no material placeholder, no
  type parameter, no comment about a future material.
- Both build records through the current six-argument `HitRecord::new`.
- B2 adds two test functions, the plane test and the triangle test.
- `HittableList::hit` stays Copy-based on this branch.
- B2 stays held until `RESOLVED`.

## Release merge

When both plans merge into the integration branch:

- Take the union `HitRecord` and the seven-argument `HitRecord::new` above.
- Keep plan-a's borrowing `HittableList::hit`.
- Add `material: Rc<dyn Material>` to `Plane` and `Triangle` (field plus `new` argument), pass it to
  `HitRecord::new`, and pass a material in B2's two tests.
- Give the scene triangle a material - see the open decision below.

## What each may rely on

- plan-b may rely on the six-argument `HitRecord::new` on its branch and on the `(u, v)` formula
  above.
- plan-a may rely on the combined record after A2.
- Neither plan adds a second `Material` trait, a placeholder material field, or a material-less
  construction path in the final product.

## Open user-owned decision (release)

The scene triangle's material changes the finished image, so the choice is the user's. Recommendation:
use the same diffuse material as plan-a's scene spheres, so the assembled scene reads consistently.
The release must ask the user, not pick silently.
########## AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/plan-a-A3+plan-b-Z1.md
# Shared design: plan-a-A3 + plan-b-Z1 (materials × geometry union)

Agreed by the plan-a and plan-b orchestrators. Both plans read this as the one copy. The
render/progress seam is settled separately in `PLANS/shared/plan-a-A3+plan-c-Z1.md`; this file adds the
hit record, the shapes, the bounding-box skip and the scene. Implementation detail only; the one
product choice it leaves open is the scene triangle's material.

## Target shape of the shared code

`src/hittable.rs` holds one `HitRecord`, not `Copy`:

```rust
pub struct HitRecord {
    pub t: f64,
    pub point: Vec3,
    /// Faces against the incoming ray.
    pub normal: Vec3,
    pub front_face: bool,
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub u: f64,
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub v: f64,
    pub material: Rc<dyn Material>,
}
```

One constructor:

```rust
pub fn new(ray: &Ray, t: f64, point: Vec3, outward_normal: Vec3, u: f64, v: f64, material: Rc<dyn Material>) -> Self
```

It sets `front_face = ray.direction.dot(outward_normal) < 0.0`, then `normal = outward_normal` when
`front_face`, otherwise `-outward_normal`.

`point` carries **no** `#[allow(dead_code)]` and no bounce-origin comment: the scatter path reads it.
`u` and `v` keep the allow because no render path reads them. `front_face` is read by glass and
`material` by the render loop, so neither carries an allow.

`Hittable` declares `hit(...)` plus the default `fn bounding_box(&self) -> Option<Aabb> { None }`.
`Sphere` and `Triangle` override it; `Plane` and `HittableList` take the default.

`HittableList::hit` - the recorded design choice, plan-a's borrow with plan-b's box skip:

```rust
let mut nearest: Option<HitRecord> = None;
for object in &self.objects {
    let limit = nearest.as_ref().map_or(t_max, |hit| hit.t);
    if let Some(bounds) = object.bounding_box() {
        if !bounds.hit(ray, t_min, limit) {
            continue;
        }
    }
    if let Some(hit) = object.hit(ray, t_min, limit) {
        nearest = Some(hit);
    }
}
nearest
```

## Shapes

- `Sphere { center, radius, material }`, `Sphere::new(center, radius, material)`. Its `hit` keeps
  plan-b's exact `(u, v)` formula and builds through the seven-argument `HitRecord::new` with
  `Rc::clone(&self.material)`. `bounding_box` returns `center - radius` to `center + radius`.
- `Plane { point, normal, material }`, `Plane::new(point, normal, material)`. Its `hit` builds through
  the seven-argument `HitRecord::new`; it takes the default `bounding_box` (`None`).
- `Triangle { a, b, c, material }`, `Triangle::new(a, b, c, material)`. Its `hit` builds through the
  seven-argument `HitRecord::new`; `bounding_box` is the corner-wise minimum and maximum.
- `src/aabb.rs` stays exactly as plan-b landed it.

## Scene

`src/main.rs` takes plan-a's material render and scene and adds plan-b's one triangle at the exact
landed vertices `(0.6, 0.15, -1.0)`, `(1.95, 0.15, -1.0)`, `(1.275, 0.92, -1.0)`. Do not move or
"improve" the placement during the merge; its measured margins are valid. The triangle's material is
the open user-owned decision below.

## Which plan changes what

**plan-a, A3, branch `plan-a`:** changes only `render`, its tests and `main` (the jittered sampling);
it does not touch `hittable.rs`, `sphere.rs`, the shapes or `main`'s scene beyond the sampling. It
records this design and needs no product change for the union, which is a release-merge concern.

**plan-b, Z1, branch `plan-b`:** changes no product code. It records this design, confirms its landed
branch, and runs its read-only closing survey and acceptance. Its branch image is **not** evidence for
the merged scene's appearance, because the triangle's material changes its colour.

## Release merge

- Take the union `HitRecord` and the seven-argument `HitRecord::new`, with the `point` allow removed.
- Take the `Hittable::bounding_box` default and the combined `HittableList::hit` above.
- `Sphere` takes material plus `bounding_box`; `Plane` and `Triangle` take material; `Aabb` is plan-b's.
- `main` takes plan-a's material render and scene plus the triangle at its exact landed vertices.
- Tests: keep one test per behavior. Drop plan-b's
  `the_center_pixel_shows_the_sphere_facing_the_camera` - its premise disappears when material
  scattering replaces normal colouring, and rewriting it as a colour assertion would be tape; the
  release's own rendered-image gate is the proof that the fixed scene still shows the sphere, and no
  replacement test is added (the test budget governs). `the_top_row_is_sky` stays. Drop plan-b's
  `the_near_surface_has_texture_coordinates_from_latitude_and_longitude`, which duplicates the `(u, v)`
  assertions plan-a's `a_ray_through_the_center_hits_the_near_surface` already makes. Plan-b's shape and
  box tests pass a material after the merge.
- Delete plan-a's `SAMPLES`/`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` per the render seam design; `DEFAULT_SAMPLES` is the one
  default.

## What each may rely on

- plan-a may rely on the record and shape shapes above after the merge.
- plan-b may rely on its branch staying read-only until the release.
- Neither plan adds a second record path, a second list loop, a second box test, a second material-less
  construction path, or a second generator.

## Open user-owned decision (release)

The scene triangle's material changes the finished image, so the choice is the user's. Recommendation:
a Lambertian in the scene spheres' family, so the triangle reads as part of the scene. The release asks
the user, not pick silently.
########## AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS/PLANS/shared/plan-a-A3+plan-c-Z1.md
# Shared design: plan-a-A3 + plan-c-Z1 (jittered samples × progress line)

Agreed by the plan-a and plan-c orchestrators. Both plans read this as the one copy. It settles
implementation detail only; it opens no user-owned decision, because jittered sampling (requirement
5) and the progress line (requirement 13) are already user-approved requirements.

## Target shape of the shared code

The merged `render` in `src/main.rs` takes plan-a's scene, camera, generator and `ray_colour`, and
plan-c's progress write:

```rust
/// Every pixel's colour, row by row from the top, each pixel averaging `samples` jittered rays, with
/// the share of finished rows reported on standard error.
fn render(width: usize, height: usize, samples: usize) -> Vec<Colour> {
    let world = scene();
    let camera = Camera::new(width as f64 / height as f64);
    let mut rng = Rng::new(SEED);
    let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity(width * height);
    for row in (0..height).rev() {
        for column in 0..width {
            let mut pixel = Colour::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
            for _ in 0..samples {
                let u = (column as f64 + rng.next_f64()) / width as f64;
                let v = (row as f64 + rng.next_f64()) / height as f64;
                pixel = pixel + ray_colour(&camera.ray(u, v), &world, &mut rng);
            }
            pixels.push(pixel / samples as f64);
        }
        let done = height - row;
        eprint!("\r{}%", done * 100 / height);
    }
    eprintln!();
    pixels
}
```

- **Progress:** the three progress lines keep plan-c's exact form and position: the `done`/`eprint!`
  pair is the last statement before the row loop's closing brace, after the column loop, and the
  single `eprintln!()` follows the row loop. A3 edits only the `render` doc comment among plan-c's
  landed lines.
- **Doc comment:** exactly the one sentence above. It is the only doc-comment sentence for `render`.
- **Jitter mapping:** `u` and `v` are drawn inside the sample loop as
  `(column + rng.next_f64()) / width` and `(row + rng.next_f64()) / height`, `u` first, then `v`,
  before that sample's scattering draws. This replaces plan-c's unjittered `(width - 1)` mapping.
- **Samples:** the merged code has no `SAMPLES` constant and no `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` constants. The single
  default is plan-c's `DEFAULT_SAMPLES = 16` (beside `DEFAULT_WIDTH = 400` and `DEFAULT_HEIGHT =
  200`), and `main` -> `run` passes `settings.samples` into `render`. `render` carries no sample-count
  validation: `parse_args` is the single validation path and rejects a count below 1.

## Which plan changes what

**plan-a, A3, branch `plan-a`:**

- Adds plan-a's `const SAMPLES: usize = 16` beside `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`; that constant is this branch's
  local default only, and its one use is the `main` call `render(WIDTH, HEIGHT, SAMPLES)`.
- Changes `render` to average `samples` jittered rays per pixel with the one `Rng::new(SEED)` created
  before both loops, using the jitter mapping above.
- Drops the planned `assert!(samples > 0)`; `render` does not validate the count.
- Replaces the `render` doc comment with the one agreed sentence, and only that clause about progress
  is added to what A3 would otherwise write.
- Adapts `the_top_row_is_sky` to the literal call `let pixels = render(200, 100, 16);` (byte-identical
  to plan-c's landed line) and keeps its assertion unchanged.
- Adds its two new tests with literal calls only: `render(20, 10, 2)` twice for
  `two_renders_with_the_same_options_give_the_same_pixels`, and `render(20, 10, 1)` versus
  `render(20, 10, 4)` for `the_sample_count_changes_the_pixels`. No test names or calls
  `WIDTH`, `HEIGHT` or `SAMPLES`.
- Does not touch the module header, `mod` list, `main` beyond the sample argument, the writers,
  `to_byte`, the scene, the materials or any output behaviour.

**plan-c, Z1r, branch `plan-c`:**

- Changes no product code. Z1r records this design, confirms plan-c's landed `render` seam and its
  frozen contract, and re-runs plan-c's acceptance render; plan-c's own branch keeps the unjittered
  loop and its existing doc sentence until the merge, because jitter is plan-a's work.
- The closing survey note and the user's acceptance of it stay as they are.

## Release merge

When plan-a and plan-c merge into the integration branch:

- Take plan-a's `scene`, `ray_colour`, `Rng`, `SEED`, `MAX_BOUNCES` and `to_byte` gamma body, with
  plan-c's `pub(crate)` on `to_byte` so `png::write_png` shares it.
- Take plan-c's module header (`//! Render a fixed scene and write it to a file as a PNG or PPM
  image.`), `mod png;`, `Format`, `Settings`, `USAGE`, `DEFAULT_WIDTH`, `DEFAULT_HEIGHT`,
  `DEFAULT_SAMPLES`, `DEFAULT_OUTPUT`, `parse_args`, `parse_dimension`, `resolve_format`, `run`,
  `main` and the progress write.
- Take the merged `render` above, including the agreed doc sentence.
- Delete plan-a's `SAMPLES`, `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` constants; plan-c has no such constants.
- The test module after the merge holds `the_top_row_is_sky`,
  `two_renders_with_the_same_options_give_the_same_pixels` and
  `the_sample_count_changes_the_pixels`. plan-c's
  `the_center_pixel_shows_the_sphere_facing_the_camera` does not survive, because materials replaced
  normal colouring in A1; plan-a's branch already dropped it.
- `tests/cli.rs` is plan-c's and needs no change: PNG-versus-PPM pixel equality is material-agnostic.

```rust
/// Every pixel's colour, row by row from the top, each pixel averaging `samples` jittered rays, with
/// the share of finished rows reported on standard error.
fn render(width: usize, height: usize, samples: usize) -> Vec<Colour> {
    let world = scene();
    let camera = Camera::new(width as f64 / height as f64);
    let mut rng = Rng::new(SEED);
    let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity(width * height);
    for row in (0..height).rev() {
        for column in 0..width {
            let mut pixel = Colour::new(0.0, 0.0, 0.0);
            for _ in 0..samples {
                let u = (column as f64 + rng.next_f64()) / width as f64;
                let v = (row as f64 + rng.next_f64()) / height as f64;
                pixel = pixel + ray_colour(&camera.ray(u, v), &world, &mut rng);
            }
            pixels.push(pixel / samples as f64);
        }
        let done = height - row;
        eprint!("\r{}%", done * 100 / height);
    }
    eprintln!();
    pixels
}
```

# Requirements

A small raytracer with no dependencies beyond the Rust standard library. It renders one fixed scene
and writes the image to a file. Every render is reproducible: the same options give the same bytes.

## Materials

1. Every object has a material. A ray that hits an object scatters by that material and the colour
   is the material's attenuation times the colour the scattered ray sees, up to a bounce limit of
   50; a ray that reaches the limit is black.
2. Diffuse material scatters in a random direction around the surface normal and attenuates by its
   albedo.
3. Metal material reflects about the normal, blurred by a fuzz factor in 0..=1, and attenuates by
   its albedo. A reflection that points into the surface is absorbed.
4. Glass material refracts by its refractive index using Snell's law, reflects on total internal
   reflection, and chooses reflection by Schlick's approximation otherwise. It does not attenuate.
5. Each pixel averages a configurable number of samples (default 16), jittered inside the pixel,
   with gamma 2 correction on output.
6. All randomness comes from the seeded generator in `src/rng.rs`, seeded with a fixed value.

## Geometry

7. Every hit records whether the ray hit the front face, and the normal always points against the
   ray.
8. Every hit records texture coordinates `(u, v)` in 0..=1: spheres by latitude and longitude,
   planes by the hit point's position along two axes in the plane, modulo 1, and triangles by their
   barycentric coordinates.
9. The scene can hold infinite planes (a point and a normal) and triangles (three vertices).
10. Every object reports an axis-aligned bounding box, and the scene list tests a ray against an
    object's box before the object. An infinite plane has no box and is always tested.

## Output and command line

11. The image is written as PNG, with no external crate: one IDAT chunk holding zlib data made of
    stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks, with correct CRC-32 and Adler-32 checksums. PPM stays
    available.
12. The command line takes `--width`, `--height`, `--samples`, `--output <path>` and
    `--format png|ppm`. The defaults are 400 by 200, 16 samples, `render.png` and the format from the
    output file's extension. An unknown option or a bad value prints a usage line and exits with a
    non-zero status.
13. While rendering, a progress line on standard error shows the share of rows done.

## Quality

14. `cargo build`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

Working plans live here. A plan is a **folder**, not a single file.

## Folder convention

```
PLANS/shared/<pair>.md  # an overlap design two parallel plans agreed on, one copy for both
PLANS/<slug>/         # <slug> is the plan's branch and worktree name; never `shared` or `archive`
  full-plan.md        # scope, design rules, and the phase status table (single source of truth)
  scope.md            # the plan's work fence, injected into every agent working on the plan
  handoff.md          # the plan orchestrator's living handoff; children never read it
  autonomous-decisions.md  # orchestrator-only working record, created when a decision needs recording
  docs-pass.md        # items explicitly deferred to the release, kept until the release clears them
  phases/<id>.md      # one detailed, implementation-grade phase — created only when that phase is active
  done/<id>.md        # a completed phase compressed to its frozen contract
  benchmarks/<name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md  # dated experiment/result/run notes (immutable records)
```

- `/plan-new` creates the plan folder with its starting `full-plan.md`, `scope.md` and
  `handoff.md`, together with the plan's branch and worktree. `/shadow-plan` does the same from the
  filled shadow templates in `../PLANNING/plan-templates/shadow/`.

- Expand the active phase into one `phases/<id>.md` file just before building it (see

  stays `active` until the retest passes.

  `benchmarks/`, never the plan root or `phases/`. They are frozen evidence: cite them from
  `full-plan.md` as `benchmarks/<note>.md` and from `done/` as `../benchmarks/<note>.md`.
  Plan-scope working documents that are not run records (for example a scope/review note

A small raytracer in Rust 2021 with no dependencies beyond the standard library. It renders one
